message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.68,"fairness_assessment":"A ranked-choice or score vote treats the three budget strategies symmetrically and captures both primary preferences and support for a balanced option; fairness improves if the club first agrees on criteria such as educational need, recruitment impact, cost, and measurable outcomes.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"Agent A","position":"Allocate the full 2000 euros to an inter-city tournament with food and prizes to increase visibility and recruit members.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"Agent B","position":"Allocate the full 2000 euros to durable educational equipment because the current boards and teaching resources are worn; this position won the debate.","influence":0.40},{"agent":"Agent C","position":"Split the budget equally between a smaller tournament and educational equipment to balance outreach and pedagogy.","influence":0.27}],"recommended_resolution":"collaborative","governance_reasoning":"Use a transparent social-choice process, preferably ranked-choice or score voting, after jointly defining success criteria. Agent B has the strongest evidenced immediate need, while A identifies a legitimate strategic objective and C offers a possible bridge. A conditional compromise—prioritizing essential equipment and funding a modest, measurable outreach event if resources permit—can preserve fairness and enable review after results are assessed."}
